versions.text: וְיֹאהַב רֵעָיו וּשְׁאָר כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל אַהֲבָה שְׁלֵמָה, לְקַיֵּם מָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא יט יח): ״וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ״. וְזֶהוּ כְּלָל גָּדוֹל בַּתּוֹרָה: דַּעֲלָךְ סָנֵי – לְחַבְרָךְ לָא תַּעֲבֵד (שבת לא א). וְגָדוֹל מִזֶּה (בראשית ט ו): ״כִּי בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם״ (ירושלמי נדרים ט ו).

versions.versionTitle: Orchot Tzaddikim, trans. Seymour J. Cohen, Ktav Pub House, 1982
versions.text: A man should love his friends and all those near to him as well as the rest of Israel with a complete love to fulfill what is said: "And you shall love your neighbor as yourself" (Lev. 19:18). And this is a great general rule in the Torah: "That which is hateful to you do not do to your neighbor" (Shabbath 31a). And even more pertinent is the verse: "For in the image of God made He man" (Gen. 9:6). (This is commented upon in T.P. Nedarim 9:4.)
